proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true admission lag shifts within-season or differs from 2 weeks, forecasts can become phase-shifted (peak timing error) and amplitude may be biased.
proposals.rationale: Baseline anchored to prior best and analyst constraint: SEIRS provides needed waning/reinfection flexibility for high-peak, high-scale dynamics; delayed_I with 2-week lag matches hospitalization-rate reporting semantics and previously showed strongest performance.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag is closer to 2 weeks, a 3-week delay can over-shift the curve, producing late peaks and degraded short-horizon tracking.
proposals.rationale: Minimal bracketing test around the 2-week anchor to assess sensitivity to slightly longer hospitalization lag while keeping the same SEIRS fractional dynamics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May be less flexible in capturing sharp peaks/long tails; can underfit peakiness or misrepresent decay, leading to systematic under/over-shoot around the peak.
proposals.rationale: Controlled ablation to isolate the effect of fractional vs non-fractional dynamics while holding structure and observation/lag fixed at the best-known configuration.
